cases.name: Tanasia Parker
cases.about:
Family members of Parker spoke to News19 Monday. 

They call Parker “Nay-Nay” and describe her as warm, outgoing, and full of love for her son.

“She just loved her son,” said Parker’s grandmother, Brenda Holloman. “She was just a lovely person. When she met people, you’d think she had known them all her life. She didn’t see color.”

“Nay-Nay always was a funny, jokey person,” said her cousin, Angel Carter. “She wanted to make people laugh. She liked to party.”

“When I think about her, I think about the song she sang, and how she was such a giving person,” said Jacqueline McDuffie, Parker’s aunt. “I just can’t think of her gone. I keep thinking this is a nightmare.”

Families members also shared some special memories they have with Parker.

"She played basketball for my son. And he used to say, Now, Nay-Nay, I put you on the team because you a family member, but you cannot play basketball. He said, You cannot," McDuffie affectionately recalled.
